long_biography.plain_text:
Before setting up his own investment platform, Brook Lenfest worked in business development at Suburban Cable, the company built by his father Gerry. He was a major shareholder when the family cable enterprise was sold in 2000. The sale gave him capital to pursue new communications and property interests, although the route by which he obtained his original shares has not been publicly described.

Lenfest invested in the regional provider NetCarrier and backed its expansion through acquisitions. He later established a private office that evolved into LGL Partners, while developing properties in Philadelphia and elsewhere. In 2026 he handed NetCarrier's day-to-day management to a new chief executive but remained its active chairman. Through the Brook J. Lenfest Foundation, he funds educational access and workforce preparation, including scholarships for students facing financial barriers.
